artists.biography: Electronic were an alternative dance supergroup formed by New Order singer and guitarist Bernard Sumner and ex-Smiths guitarist Johnny Marr. They co-wrote the majority of their output between 1989 and 1998, collaborating with Neil Tennant and Chris Lowe, of the Pet Shop Boys, on three tracks in their early years, and former Kraftwerk member Karl Bartos on nine songs in 1995.

perplexity.description:
Released in 1991, Electronic is the debut studio album by the British alternative dance supergroup Electronic, formed by Bernard Sumner of New Order and Johnny Marr of The Smiths. The album blends electronic music with guitar-driven rock, combining Sumner’s synth-pop sensibilities and Marr’s melodic guitar work. The sound is characterized by lush production, danceable beats, and emotionally resonant songwriting, with notable contributions from Neil Tennant and Chris Lowe of Pet Shop Boys on several tracks. Key singles like "Get the Message" and "Getting Away With It" showcase the band’s ability to merge synth-pop textures with rock energy, while songs such as "Soviet" and "Feel Every Beat" reflect both personal and political themes.

Electronic holds a significant place in the discography of both Sumner and Marr, marking a departure from their previous bands while retaining elements of their signature styles. The album was critically acclaimed upon release, praised for its ambitious fusion of genres and its fresh take on the electronic-rock hybrid. Commercially, it was a major success, reaching No. 2 in the UK and selling over a million copies worldwide. Its impact was further solidified by the Top 10 hit "Get the Message" and the enduring popularity of tracks like "Feel Every Beat," cementing Electronic as a standout release in the early 1990s electronic and alternative rock scenes.
